verdict.rationale: Both changes move the email, name and role checks into one module and keep the message wording and order. A also lowercases invitation emails, as `docs/api.md` requires, and reports this as its one behavior change. B keeps that bug and adds a `lowercase: false` option just to preserve it. A also adds focused tests for the shared validators and for the invitation edge cases, while B adds no tests to protect the refactor.
a_issues: Changes `inviteUser` behavior (lowercasing emails) inside a refactor task, though it is justified by the docs and clearly reported.
`validateOptionalName` and `validateName` split the name rule into two exported functions instead of one parameterized function. This is minor.
b_issues: Keeps the documented bug in `inviteUser`: emails are not lowercased, so invitations differing only in case are not caught as duplicates, contrary to `docs/api.md`.
The `lowercase: false` option exists only to preserve that bug, which adds an escape hatch that undermines the shared rule.
`INVITABLE_ROLES` stays hardcoded in `inviteUser` instead of being derived from the shared `ROLES`, so the two lists can drift apart.
Adds no tests for the new validation module or the refactored handlers.
